title: Bridge mode for legacy streaming with opt-in modern toolcall semantics
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Several large customers still rely on our older streaming envelope semantics and an early tool-call glue that embeds tool metadata inline with tokens. When we introduced the newer structured toolcalling API and stricter streaming envelopes, some clients observed partial truncation, duplicate end-of-stream markers, and malformed tool invocation signals. Goal: Introduce a runtime "bridge mode" that allows legacy streaming semantics and the new toolcall schema to coexist for targeted customers while we provide migration tooling and a clear deprecation timeline. The bridge must be controllable via behavior flags per-tenant, observable in Console, covered by automated replay/backcompat tests, and have a low-risk rollout plan with fast rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Flagged bridge mode can be enabled per-customer via config and takes effect without server restart
Legacy streaming envelopes are normalized to the modern schema by the bridge for downstream consumers
Tool invocations emitted under legacy inline form are translated to the structured toolcall events when bridge mode is enabled
Integration tests exercise every streaming + toolcall permutation (legacy -> legacy, legacy -> modern, modern -> legacy, modern -> modern) and pass in the CI gate
Canary rollout dashboard shows token-level divergence metrics and error spikes and supports automatic rollback if error-rate > 3% for 10 minutes
proposed_solution: Add a translator layer in the serving runtime that can be toggled with two tenant-level behavior flags: 'legacy_streaming_bridge' and 'toolcall_structured_compat'. In bridge mode the runtime will: 1) detect legacy envelope markers and rewrite them to the canonical streaming envelope; 2) extract inline toolcall payloads and emit canonical structured toolcall events (with schema v2) without mutating the persisted model state; 3) attach translation metadata to traces so we can audit rewrites. Provide a migration CLI that scans recorded session logs and outputs a report with the number of affected messages and suggested client changes. Tests include unit converters, simulated network replays, and an E2E suite running against a local dedicated pool. Rollout: start with internal customers and a blind canary (2% traffic) then expand to opted-in customers before scheduled deprecation window.
implementation_steps: Design translator and define translation rules (edge cases, ambiguous markers)
Implement translator module in runtime streaming stack with feature flags
Add tenant-level flag controls to control plane and surface in Console
Build migration CLI and a lightweight replayer for historical sessions
Write contract/backcompat tests and add to CI gate
Run internal canary, iterate on metrics, then invite pilot customers
Publish migration guide and schedule deprecation calendar with PM
risks: Silent mis-translation could corrupt client-side tool invocations leading to incorrect downstream actions
Performance overhead of translation under high-throughput workloads might increase p99 latency
Complex edge cases where legacy inline payloads are ambiguous and human review is required
Rollout coordination burden across Dedicated and Private deployments where flag propagation is slower
